subject: POC environment recommendation + staging runbook for HealthPlus trial
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthplus.com>, Olivia Cheng <olivia.cheng@healthplus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC environment recommendation + staging runbook for HealthPlus trial

Hi Sanjay / Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + my recommendation for the POC environment so we can get you testing end-to-end by the week of May 3.

Recap of key goals you shared:
- 5000 daily inference calls across patient messaging and triage flows
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for single-turn generation
- Data residency: customer data cannot leave HealthPlus VPC during the trial
- Success criteria: functional parity on canonical prompts (accuracy/SAFETY), cost estimate within 20% of projected, and no data exfiltration in logs

Recommended environment (my read based on constraints):
1) Private VPC trial (preferred) — Customer-managed VPC peering + private endpoints to Redwood Private control plane. Pros: satisfies data residency, closest to production network topology. Cons: longer setup (network ops + firewall rules).
2) Dedicated sandbox (fallback) — Redwood-managed dedicated capacity in our US region with VPN tunnel and strict egress controls. Pros: faster spin-up (~3 business days), predictable throughput. Cons: requires Data Processing Addendum + temporary data handling exceptions.
3) Hosted (not recommended) — does not meet explicit residency requirement.

Immediate next steps / asks (owners):
- Sanjay / Olivia: confirm preference for VPC trial vs Dedicated sandbox by EOD Mon 4/26 (external owner)
- Procurement (cc): if VPC, please complete the MSA addendum pages we shared; start legal review — link in related links (external owner)
- Karthik: can you confirm rough infra checklist + a minimal runbook for VPC peering and private endpoints? (internal owner)
- Marissa: once Karthik confirms, please propose a short test-plan (canonical prompts + smoke tests) we can run during week 1 of the trial (internal owner)

Attachments: redwood-poc-success-criteria.pdf (draft success criteria), hp-network-requirements-stub.txt (what we need from your network team)

Timeline goal: agree environment by 4/26 -> kickoff network setup 4/27 -> ready for smoke tests by 5/3.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15m follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Dylan

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthplus.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC environment recommendation + staging runbook for HealthPlus trial

Thanks Dylan — good summary. After talking to our security and network leads we prefer option 1 (Private VPC trial). Key points from our side:
- Security will require a read-only flow for logs to a customer-managed S3 within our VPC (no logs stored in Redwood-hosted buckets)
- We'll need a short risk doc for legal (can you share the MPA template + redline guidance?)
- If network work looks heavy, we can consider the dedicated sandbox as a Plan B but prefer to try VPC first

I'll confirm the internal owners by Friday. Procurement looped in to start the MSA addendum review.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Director, Digital Ops | HealthPlus Care
sanjay@healthplus.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthplus.com>, Olivia Cheng <olivia.cheng@healthplus.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: POC environment recommendation + staging runbook for HealthPlus trial

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding HealthPlus confirmation that they want to attempt a Private VPC trial. Can you please respond with the minimal infra checklist and any gotchas (firewall rules, NAT, DNS, certs) we need to hand to their networking team? High level items we expect:
- VPC peering / Transit Gateway requirements
- Subnet ranges and IP allowlist (we need their egress IPs)
- Ports: 443 outbound to Private endpoints + 4500/500 for any IPSec VPN if they prefer
- TLS cert requirements and SNI expectations
- Logging pattern: we need to support log forwarding to an S3 bucket they control (read-only) and confirm we will not persist PII on Redwood-managed buckets during the trial

Can you reply with a 1-page runbook + an estimated timeline to complete the network hands-on together? Goal is to send to them tomorrow so procurement/legal can start parallel review.

Thanks — Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthplus.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC environment recommendation + staging runbook for HealthPlus trial

Adding a quick plan from the ops side — draft runbook below. Karthik, flag any changes.

Minimal VPC trial runbook (1 page draft):
- Step 0: Pre-checks (timeline: 1 business day)
  - Confirm CIDR blocks (no overlap) and provide Redwood egress IPs
  - Exchange public key + contact for networking window
- Step 1: Network connectivity (timeline: 1–3 business days)
  - Establish VPN/IPSec or Transit Gateway peering based on their preference
  - Open outbound 443 to priv-endpoints.redwood.internal and allow return traffic
- Step 2: Private endpoints & certs (timeline: 1 day once connectivity is up)
  - We will issue a cert for the private endpoint; HealthPlus must add internal DNS entry or hosts entry during test window
- Step 3: Logging & storage (timeline: 1 day)
  - Configure log-forwarder to push request logs to customer S3 (read-only) — provide IAM role policy stub (attachment)
  - Confirm retention window (we will honor 30-day retention by default for trial)
- Step 4: Smoke tests (timeline: target 5/3)
  - Run canonical prompts and latency checks (Marissa to run)
  - If p95 passes and logs look good, sign off for expanded sample testing

Deliverables we will send today: 1) one-page runbook, 2) IAM policy stub, 3) draft success criteria (attached). Estimated total setup time: 3–5 business days assuming network team availability.

Marissa
